drug_class: Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator (CFTR) Modulator Combination
purpose: This medication is used to treat cystic fibrosis (CF) in patients who have at least one copy of a specific gene mutation called F508del. It helps improve lung function and overall quality of life for people living with CF. Your doctor will confirm if your specific gene type responds to this treatment.
how_it_works: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a faulty protein in your body that disrupts how salt and water move in and out of your cells, leading to thick, sticky mucus in your lungs. Tezacaftor helps the faulty protein fold and reach the right place in the cell, while ivacaftor helps that protein work better once it gets there. Together, they team up to improve how the protein functions, helping to thin out that mucus and make breathing easier.
common_side_effects: Headache, nausea, dizziness, stuffy or runny nose, sore throat, stomach pain, rash, and increases in liver enzymes. Some people may also notice respiratory symptoms like a cough or shortness of breath, especially at the start of treatment.
warnings: This medicine can affect your liver, so your doctor will check your liver with blood tests before and during treatment. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking this medication. It can also interact with certain other medications, especially ones that affect liver enzymes, so always share your full medication list with your pharmacist or doctor.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one combination tablet of tezacaftor 100 mg and ivacaftor 150 mg taken in the morning with fat-containing food (like eggs or butter), plus one separate ivacaftor 150 mg tablet taken in the evening, also with food. It is important to take it with a fatty meal to help your body absorb the medicine properly. Always follow the exact instructions your doctor gives you.
